You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

> limited to deregistration filings and the subsequent public filers in the chain of
> ownership. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was
> structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status of the acquired entity (feasibility-relevant)
- On July 30, 2018, RSP Permian, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of
  registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act and
  suspension of its duty to file reports under Sections 13(a)/15(d); the filing recorded
  approximately 1 holder of record as of the certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-231571, Form 15-12B]
- A search of RSP Permian, Inc.'s (CIK 0001588216) EDGAR filing history for annual
  reports finds no Form 10-K filed after the pre-merger FY2017 10-K (filed 2018-02-27);
  no periodic report covering fiscal years within the ~2021-2023 outcome window was
  located. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001588216&type=10-K]

## Public-reporting status of the direct acquirer (Concho Resources Inc.)
- Concho Resources Inc. (CIK 0001358071) continued as an SEC-reporting filer after the
  RSP merger, but its last annual report as an independent registrant was its Form 10-K
  for fiscal year 2019, filed February 19, 2020 — approximately 1.5 years after the RSP
  merger closed and before the start of the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001358071-20-000011, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- On January 15, 2021, ConocoPhillips completed its previously announced acquisition of
  Concho: Falcon Merger Sub Corp. (a wholly owned ConocoPhillips subsidiary) merged with
  and into Concho pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated October 18, 2020,
  with Concho becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of ConocoPhillips; each Concho share was
  converted into the right to receive 1.46 shares of ConocoPhillips common stock. In
  connection with the merger, Concho requested that NYSE withdraw the listing of its
  common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-21-004795, Form 8-K]
- Concho subsequently filed a Form 15-12B on January 29, 2021 to terminate its own
  registration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-21-009083, Form 15-12B]
- Because Concho itself deregistered on January 29, 2021 — before the fixed ~2021-2023
  outcome window is reached in any of Concho's own periodic filings — no Concho-level
  10-K exists within the window that could separately disclose the trajectory of the
  RSP-derived asset base. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-21-009083, Form 15-12B]

## Status of the acquired entity within the ultimate parent (ConocoPhillips)
- ConocoPhillips' (CIK 0001163165) Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021, filed February 17,
  2022, lists "RSP Permian, Inc." and "RSP Permian, L.L.C." (both Delaware entities)
  among its subsidiaries in Exhibit 21.1. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-22-000031, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21.1 "Subsidiaries of the Registrant"]
- The same two entities, "RSP Permian, Inc." and "RSP Permian, L.L.C.," both Delaware,
  continue to be listed among ConocoPhillips' subsidiaries in Exhibit 21 of its Form
  10-K for fiscal year 2022 (filed February 16, 2023) and its Form 10-K for fiscal year
  2023 (filed February 15, 2024). [SRC: SEC accession 0001163165-23-000006, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21] [SRC: SEC accession 0001163165-24-000010, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21]
- The Exhibit 21 subsidiary listings give only entity name and state of incorporation;
  they contain no financial, operating, or headcount data specific to these entities.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-22-000031, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21.1]

## Items sought but not found
- No source was located in which ConocoPhillips' Form 10-K narrative (business,
  properties, or segment-reporting sections) or financial statements, within the
  ~2021-2023 window, separately breaks out the RSP-derived Permian Basin acreage or its
  financial results from ConocoPhillips' consolidated Permian Basin/Lower 48 operations.
  [UNVERIFIED]
- No reputable-press or primary source was located reporting a divestiture, impairment,
  write-down, or comparable outcome scalar specifically tied to the RSP-derived asset
  base (as distinct from Concho's or ConocoPhillips' consolidated Permian Basin results)
  within the ~2021-2023 window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- RSP Permian, Inc. deregistered in July 2018 and never again filed as a public
  reporting company; its direct acquirer, Concho Resources Inc., itself deregistered in
  January 2021 upon being absorbed into ConocoPhillips, before Concho's own periodic
  reporting reached the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-231571, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-21-009083, Form 15-12B]
- Within the ~2021-2023 window, the only traceable public record of the acquired legal
  entities is their continued listing as Delaware subsidiaries of ConocoPhillips in
  three consecutive years of Exhibit 21 filings (FY2021-FY2023), with no accompanying
  financial or operating disclosure specific to them. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-22-000031, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21.1] [SRC: SEC accession 0001163165-23-000006, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21] [SRC: SEC accession 0001163165-24-000010, Form 10-K, Exhibit 21]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome: the
  acquired business passed through two successive absorptions (into Concho, then into
  ConocoPhillips) without any intervening or subsequent public filer isolating its own
  3-5-year financial or operating trajectory.

[SLICE END]
